Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:10:1.english: One who purchases produce from another - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:10:2.hebrew: ואם היו צרורין - הוי סימן, או קשר או מנין שבהם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:10:2.english: And if they were bundled - [This] is a distinguishing mark, either the knot or the count [of coins] in them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:11:1.english: Rabbi Elazar says: Even [if they are] placed upon a table - It seems to me that we do not have the reading "bound."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:13:1.hebrew: לתני על גבי שולחן - של שולחני, וכ"ש בין הכסא ולשולחני:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:13:1.english: Let [the Tanna] teach "upon the table" - [that they belong] to the money changer, and all the more so [coins found] between the chair and the money changer.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:13:2.hebrew: אי נמי - ניתני ברישא "מצא בשולחנות" כדקתני רישא "מצא בחנות". מדנקט "לפני השולחני", אף על השולחן במשמע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:13:2.english: Or else - let [the mishna] teach in the first clause, "found in the money-changing establishment," just as the first clause teaches, "found in a store." Since it states "before the money changer," even "on the table" is implied.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:1:1.hebrew: נקיטנא ליה כו' - משבענא ליה שבועת היסת, ולא נתייאש מיד כשמשמש ולא מצא, ונמצא שבא ליד זה לפני יאוש. והלכה כאביי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:1:1.english: I will seize him, etc. - I will administer an oath of hesset [a rabbinic oath] to him, and [thus] he does not despair immediately when he feels [for it] and does not find [it]; so it turns out that it came into this [finder's] hand before despair. And the halakha is in accordance with Abaye.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:2:1.hebrew: אי נקיטנא וכו' - ואינו יכול להשביעו בטענת שמא, שאין נשבעין בטענת שמא אלא אותן השנויין במשנה "ואלו נשבעים שלא בטענה" כו' (שבועות דף מה.). וא"ת: הא מקמי יאוש אתי לידיה, ואוקימנא הלכתא כאביי ביע"ל קג"ם? הא אמרן דמעות מידע ידיע מיד, כרבי יצחק דאמר: אדם עשוי למשמש בכיסו כו' (לעיל בבא מציעא דף כא:):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:2:1.english: If I seize, etc. - And he cannot impose an oath upon him based on a claim of uncertainty, because one does not take an oath on a claim of uncertainty except [in] those [cases] taught in the Mishnah [beginning] "And these take an oath without a [definite] claim," etc. (Shevuot 45a). And if you ask: Behold, [the coin] came into [the finder's] hand before despair, and we have established the halakha in accordance with Abaye in [the mnemonic] Ya'al Kagam [that unwitting despair is not valid despair]? [The answer is that] we have already said that coins are known [to have been lost] immediately, in accordance with Rabbi Yitzchak, who said: A person is accustomed to feel his pocket, etc. (above, Bava Metzia 21b).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:3:1.hebrew: אימור שותפי נינהו - בסלע זו, ונאמנים זה על זה, ואין האחד חושד את חבירו בחלקו. ולכי מישמש בכיסו ולא מצאה, לא אייאש; מימר אמר: אחד מן השותפים מצאה, ולצערני הוא שותק. ונמצא, כשבאת ליד זה, לפני יאוש באת לידו, והא אוקמיה כאביי; הלכך, אע"ג דסלע דבר שאין בו סימן הוא, חייב להחזיר. אבל כי אין בו שלש פרוטות, מה נפשך: אי שותפין הן בו, אין כאן משום השבת אבידה; ואם של אחד מהם הוא או של השנים, נואשו, ואמרו: חברנו זה גנב הוא, והרי משמט ואמר "לא לקחתיו" — אחד מכם לקחו וגנבו מחבירו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:3:1.english: Say [that perhaps] they are partners - in this sela, and they trust one another, and one does not suspect his fellow regarding his portion. And when he feels in his pocket and does not find it, he does not despair; [rather,] he says [to himself]: "One of the partners found it, and it is [only] to distress me that he is keeping silent." Thus it turns out that when it came into this [finder's] hand, it came into his hand before despair, and behold, we have [already] established it in accordance with Abaye; therefore, even though a sela is an item that has no distinguishing mark, he is obligated to return [it]. However, when there are not three perutot in it, whichever way you look at it: if they are partners in it, there is no [obligation] here on account of returning a lost item; and if it belongs to one of them or to two [of them], they despair, and they say: "This companion of ours is a thief, and behold, he is evading [it] and saying, 'I did not take it' — one of you took it and stole it from his fellow!"

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:3:2.hebrew: אימור שותפי נינהו - ומהימני אהדדי, ואין חושדין זה את זה, ונמצאת שבאת ליד זה לפני יאוש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:3:2.english: Say they are partners - And they trust one another and do not suspect each other, and thus it turns out that [it] came into this [finder's] hand before [the owners'] despair.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:5:1.english: He saw a sela that fell - And we do not read [the word] “from two [people]” [in the text].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:5:2.english: He took it before despair - [That is,] he did not wait [long enough] for this [owner] to feel in his pocket.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:6:1.hebrew: עובר משום השב תשיבם - לא תגזול לא שייך אלא בשעת נטילה, כמו ויגזול את החנית מיד המצרי (שמואל ב כג), כדאמר בבבא קמא (עט.). לא תוכל להתעלם אינה אזהרה אלא לכובש את עיניו ונמנע מלהציל. הלכך, הנוטלה על מנת להחזיר ולאחר יאוש נתכוין לגוזלה — אין כאן מתעלם, אבל השב תשיבם איכא, משנטל עד שישיבנה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:6:1.english: He violates [a commandment] due to “You shall surely return them” - [The prohibition] “You shall not rob” applies only at the time of taking, as [in the verse,] “and he snatched the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand” (II Samuel 23[:21]), as stated in Bava Kamma (79a). [The prohibition] “You may not disregard [it]” is a warning only for one who averts his eyes and refrains from rescuing [the lost item]. Therefore, [regarding] one who takes it in order to return [it], and after despair [of the owner] intended to steal it — there is no [violation of] “disregarding” here, but [the obligation of] “You shall surely return them” applies from when he took [it] until he returns it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:7:1.english: He waited for it, etc. - At the time that he saw it and did not take it to return it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:7:2.english: He violates "You may not disregard" - For he hid his eyes [from it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:8:1.english: Into the sand - Among the sands.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:9:1.hebrew: מצא בחנות הרי אלו שלו - בדבר שאין בו סימן קאי, דההוא דנפל מיניה מיאש, שהכל נכנסים לשם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:9:1.english: [If one] found [items] in a store, these are his - [The Mishnah] refers to an item that has no distinguishing mark, for the one from whom it fell despairs [of recovering it], since everyone enters there.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:9:2.hebrew: בין התיבה - שהחנוני יושב לפניה, ותמיד נוטל ממנה ונותן לפניו ומוכר, ומעות שנותנין לו נותן לתיבה, ולא נפל שום דבר אלא מיד חנוני:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:9:2.english: Between the chest - For the storekeeper sits in front of it, and constantly takes from it and places [merchandise] before him and sells [it], and the coins that they give him he puts into the chest, and nothing fell [there] except from the storekeeper's hand.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:9:3.hebrew: שולחני - מחליף מעות, ונותן מטבעותיו בשולחן שלפניו, והבאין להחליף אף הן נותנין שם מעותיהן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:9:3.english: A money changer - [One who] exchanges money, and places his coins on the table before him, and those who come to exchange [money] also place their coins there.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:9:4.hebrew: הרי אלו שלו - דאמרינן מן הבאין נפלו, שהרי השולחן מפסיק בין שולחני למעות שנמצאו. ואם מן השולחני נפלו, היה להם להמצא בינו לכסא שהשולחן מונח עליו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 26b:9:4.english: These belong to him - For we say [that] they fell from those who come [to him], since the table separates between [the] money changer and the coins that were found. And if they had fallen from the money changer, they should have been found between him and the chair upon which the table rests.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:10:1.hebrew: אפילו צרורין - רש"י ל"ג צרורין, דאם היה בו סימן, מכריז. וי"ל דגריס ליה, ומיירי דאיכא רוב עכו"ם מצויים שם, והם שלו ואע"ג דאיכא סימן, דהלכה כר' שמעון בן אלעזר בהא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:10:1.english: Even [if they are] bundled - Rashi does not have the reading "bundled," because if there were an identifying mark on it, he would [have to] proclaim [it]. And one can say that he does have that reading, and [the Mishnah] is speaking [of a case] where there is a majority of gentiles present there, and they are his even though there is an identifying mark, because the halakhah follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar in this [matter].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:1:1.hebrew: שנפל משנים חייב להחזיר - אפילו אין בו סימן, דאינו מתיאש לעולם. ומיירי ששניהם בקשוה יחד קודם שבא זה ומצאה, ולכך סבור ודאי שחבירו לקחה כשבקשה עמו, ואינו מתיאש לעולם, שמחשב: "יחזירנה לי כשאביישנו ברבים ואוכיח לו שמצאו". ולכך נמי אמרינן בסמוך: "אימור שותפי נינהו", כיון שראינום מחפשין יחד. ומה שפרש"י מטעם יאוש שלא מדעת — אין נראה, דהא רבא סבר דהוי יאוש, ומפרש בסמוך מילתיה דרב נחמן, ואין סברא לומר דהדר ביה בתר דאיתותב. ומה שפירש נמי שישביענו שבועת היסת — קשה: וכי ישביענו בטענת ספק? ומיהו י"ל דטוען ברי, לפי שלא היה שם אחר כי אם הוא. אך קשה, דבימי בר קפרא עדיין לא נתקנה שבועת היסת. ונראה לפרש שבלא שבועה אינו מתיאש לעולם, כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:1:1.english: That fell from [one of] two [people], he is obligated to return [it] - Even if it has no distinguishing mark, for he never despairs [of recovering it]. And [the Gemara] is speaking of a case where both of them searched for it together before this [finder] came and found it, and therefore [the owner] is certain that his companion took it when he searched for it with him; and he never despairs, for he thinks: "He will return it to me when I shame him in public and prove to him that he found it." And for this reason as well, [the Gemara] says shortly: "Say that they are partners," since we saw them searching together. And as for what Rashi explained, [that it is] for the reason of ye'ush shelo mida'at (unconscious despair) — this does not seem [correct], for Rava holds that it is [valid] despair, and he explains shortly the statement of Rav Nachman, and it is not reasonable to say that he retracted after he was refuted. And also what [Rashi] explained, that he will administer to him a shevu'at hesset (oath of inducement) — this is difficult: would he administer an oath to him based on an uncertain claim? However, one can say that he makes a certain claim, because no one else was there except him. Yet it is still difficult, because in the days of Bar Kappara, the shevu'at hesset had not yet been instituted. Therefore, it seems [best] to explain that even without an oath, he never despairs, as I have explained.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:3:1.hebrew: לא אמרן אלא כי לית ביה שוה פרוטה לכל חד וחד - דהיינו כי ליכא שלש פרוטות אלא ב', דמה נפשך אין צריך להחזיר: אם שלשתן שותפין — אין כאן כדי השבה לכל אחד, ואם אינן שותפין — האובד יתיאש, כי השנים ידחוהו כל אחד על חבירו. וא"ת: וניחוש שמא שנים הם שותפין, דאין חושדים זה את זה, ולא מתיאשי, ששניהם יטענו בטענת ברי לשלישי? וכן באיכא דאמרי: אמאי קאמר "הני שותפי נינהו וחד מינייהו אחיל מנתיה גבי חבריה"? נימא: אימור שנים מהם הם שותפין ואין חושדין זה את זה, ויאמרו ודאי שהשלישי לקחה? וי"ל: דודאי כי ליכא אלא שנים — האחד יטען ברי לחבירו; אבל כשיש שלשה — לא יטענו טענת ברי לשלישי, אפי' יהיו שנים מהן שותפין, דנהי דאין חושדים זה את זה, מ"מ סבור שהשותף לקחה לצערו עד זמן מרובה — כדאמר בסמוך דאי איכא שלש פרוטות, דאינם מתיאשים, שסבורים שחבריהם מצאם ומעלים מהם להקניט ולצער עד זמן מרובה, ולבסוף יחזירנה. ועי"ל: דכיון ששלשה הולכין יחד, אין לומר שותפין שנים מהם, אלא או כולם שותפין או כל אחד ואחד לבדו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:3:1.english: We said [this] only when it does not have the value of a peruta for each and every one - That is, when there are not three perutot, but only two, for either way, he does not need to return [it]: if the three of them are partners, there is not enough here for [an obligation of] returning for each one; and if they are not partners, the one who lost [it] will despair, because the two [others] will each push him off onto his fellow. And if you ask: Let us be concerned that perhaps two [of them] are partners, who do not suspect one another, and they will not despair, because the two of them will advance a definite claim against the third? And likewise in [the version of] "there are those who say": why does he say, "These are partners, and one of them relinquished his share to his fellow"? Let us say: perhaps two of them are partners, and they do not suspect one another, and they will say with certainty that the third one took it? And one can answer: Certainly when there are only two [people], the one will advance a definite claim against his fellow; however, when there are three, they will not advance a definite claim against the third even if two of them are partners, for although they do not suspect one another [of theft], nevertheless [each] thinks that [his] partner took it to vex him for a long time — as [it] says nearby, that when there are three perutot, they do not despair because they think that their fellows found [it] and are concealing [it] from them to tease and vex [them] for a long time, and in the end will return it. And one can also answer: Since three [people] are walking together, one cannot say that two of them are partners; rather, either all of them are partners, or each and every one is on his own.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:5:1.hebrew: מתנה בעלמא הוא דיהיב ליה - וא"ת: והלא לאו ד"לא תגזול" מקרי ניתק לעשה בפ' שילוח הקן (חולין דף קמא.), א"כ, כיון דלענין גזילה לא מקרי מתנה, גם "השב תשיבם" למה לא תיקן? וי"ל: דלא קאי אלא על לאו ד"לא תוכל להתעלם", שעבר שלא החזיר קודם יאוש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:5:1.english: It is merely a gift that he gave him - And if you will ask: Is not the prohibition of "You shall not rob" called [a prohibition] connected to a positive commandment in the chapter [entitled] Shiluach HaKen (Chullin 141a)? If so, since with respect to robbery it is not considered a gift, why did he also not rectify "You shall return them"? And one can answer that [Rava's statement] refers only to the prohibition of "You may not disregard," which he transgressed by not returning [it] before despair.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:6:1.hebrew: אינו עובר אלא משום השב תשיבם - ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף לד. ושם ד"ה מעקה) דחשיב השבת אבידה עשה שאין הזמן גרמא, היינו בענין שבכאן. וא"ת: ואמאי ליכא לאו ד"לא תגזול"? אי משום דבהתירא אתא לידיה, הלא בכובש שכר שכיר איכא לאו, כדאמר בפרק איזהו נשך (לקמן בבא מציעא דף סא. ושם)? וי"ל: דהתם כשמתכוין לגזול לא נתיאשו הבעלים, והכא כבר נתיאשו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 26b:6:1.english: He violates only [the commandment] of “You shall surely return them” - And in the first chapter of Kiddushin (34a, and ibid., s.v. Ma'akeh), where [the Gemara] counts returning a lost item as a positive commandment not bound by time, that is in a case like this here. And if you should ask: Why is there no prohibition of “You shall not rob”? If [you say it is] because it came into his hand permissibly, is there not a prohibition in [the case of] one who withholds a hired worker’s wages, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter Eizehu Neshekh (below, Bava Metzia 61a, and ibid.)? And one can answer: There, when he intends to steal, the owners have not despaired, whereas here, they have already despaired.
